item.title: Technical and Ethical Limits
item.lead: The technical section of the dossier concludes with a set of design questions: which automation is transparent, which data is proportionate, and which human expectation must be protected?

blocks.text: The first limit is identity transparency. The user must be able to understand whether the person with whom they are communicating is genuinely the portrayed creator, an employee, a team, or an automated assistant. The dossier considers hidden identity switching as a fundamental problem.

The second limit is data minimization. Not all information that can technically be stored necessarily needs to be commercially utilized. Especially sensitive personal data can create an asymmetry much greater than the user expects at the moment of sharing.

The third limit is purpose transparency. A system that detects emotional signals to facilitate a smoother conversation is different from a system that uses those same signals to maximize willingness to pay. The dossier states that precisely this shift constitutes the ethical core of the problem.

The fourth limit is auditability. When AI becomes part of the sales chain, prompts, logs, model output, human overrides, and decision rules must be reconstructable. Without such a trace, the technical backend remains opaque – precisely the problem that this series investigates.
